trades.holding_period_note: sessions_held is measured per closed tranche of an average-cost lot, so tranches of the same lot share its entry date and their intervals overlap; they must not be summed. sessions_in_market is the union.

costs.note_price_difference: slippage_bps / price_difference is measured against the decision mid and therefore INCLUDES intraday drift (it can be negative). execution_cost_bps is friction only.

implementation_shortfall.note: drift is the mid's own movement between decision and execution; it is a timing outcome, not a fee, and is reported separately from the friction components.

pnl_decomposition.note: Realized and open P&L are net of explicit cash costs (commission, exchange and regulatory fees less rebates), which are the only costs charged to cash separately; spread, depth and impact are already inside the fill prices. The residual is the rounding gap and is reported rather than hidden.

narrative.headline: Beat the market: +74.29% total return vs +14.41% for the index, +57.59pp residual after beta, -18.3% max drawdown, 0.82% of capital lost to execution costs.

clauses.text: Finished at +74.29% against the S&P 500's +14.41% over the same 251 sessions - an excess return of +59.87pp.
The momentum premium this participant is built to harvest was live (+22.09% over the season) and the account made money - a tailwind that cannot be separated from skill on one path.
Of the +74.29% total, about +16.69pp is explained by carrying beta 1.16 against a +14.41% market (R^2 0.19); the residual +57.59pp is everything else - selection, timing, leverage and cost.
XBI contributed +69,832 USD (94% of net P&L) across 39 closed trades; IBB was the biggest drag at +4,231 USD.
Execution cost 822 USD (0.82% of starting capital, 0.9 bp per fill, 1.4 bp of the 5,806,047 USD traded). 80% of that was spread/depth/impact and 20% was explicit fees and rebates.
46 closed round trips, 43.5% winners, profit factor 3.10, average winner +5,470 vs average loser -1,359 USD, median holding 13 sessions.

Time in market, measured without double counting: 206 sessions held at least one position (the per-tranche holding periods above sum to 859 sessions because tranches of the same average-cost lot share its entry date, so they overlap and must not be added together).
Single worst trade: XBI long 2026-02-10 to 2026-03-30, -10,142 USD.
Worst peak-to-trough drawdown -18.26% (-9.10% for the index), trough on 2026-04-06, recovered 2026-06-17. Average gross exposure 110% of starting capital, peak leverage 1.94x.
Daily returns were +0.40 skewed with excess kurtosis +1.95; historical 95% VaR -3.28%/day with CVaR -4.58%/day. Worst single session -6.31%, best +8.87%.

The style premia quoted above are measured on the simulated replay, whose cross-sectional drifts are DECLARED scenario parameters (see sim/universe.py). They describe this competition, not the real market: IR-16.

Declared failure mode(s) that actually fired: Biotech is high-beta to rates; a hot approval regime cannot beat a rate shock; Monthly-to-quarterly regime changes mean the position can be stale for weeks.
Season context: the real S&P 500 fell 9.10% from 2026-01-27 to 2026-03-30, VIX peaked at 31.05 on 2026-03-27, and cross-sectional dispersion was 103.8pp (stdev of individual 1-year returns).

prose.title: Mandate (as declared before the season)
prose.text: @FDACatalyst_Rider (FDA Catalyst Rider) ran the "post-event drift" archetype. Declared thesis: openFDA's own decision dates show when the FDA's approval flow accelerates. A hot approval regime raises the sector's expected cash-flow news and biotech re-rates with a lag; the rider holds the sector at the Reg T limit while the regime lasts. Entry: Count approvals of original applications with status AP whose decision date falls in the trailing 30 calendar days (openFDA); Enter XBI at 150% of equity when that count is at or above its trailing 252-session median; Add IBB at 40% of equity when the count exceeds the median by 25%. Exit: Flatten when the trailing-30-day count falls back below the median; No stop loss: the regime, not the drawdown, closes the position. Sizing: 150% XBI plus up to 40% IBB; 1.9x gross, Reg T initial margin 50%. Leverage: 1.9x gross. Cadence: daily check, weeks-long holds, horizon weeks. Aggression 5/5. This participant was built to maximise return, not to manage risk: Biotech sector swings are among the largest of any US industry ETF, and the signal is an official dated event stream rather than a price derivative.
